{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABZamttw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhDB7Gw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 27, "title": "Load, apply and preserve VPD bone poses through the BDEF glTF pipeline", "body": "## Problem

The converter rejects VPD workflows, and `examples/rig.ts` substitutes a hardcoded deformation preset. Users cannot load a pose, bind it reliably to converted bones, or preserve the result in glTF. BDEF conversion already retains exact source bone identity, unit scale and inverse binds, providing the necessary foundation.

## Expected outcome

Deliver a complete VPD bone-offset path across documented semantics, converter API/CLI, reusable Three.js pose APIs and Demo. Convert PMX plus VPD into posed GLB/unpacked glTF; load/apply VPD to converter-produced rigs at runtime; preserve repeatable application and reset after serialization.

Use core joint transforms for the resolved pose. Keep the existing Toon/Outline drafts and independent PBR fallback. Define any additional metadata needed for model binding, baseline recovery and diagnostics; introduce an extension only for semantics that core glTF and the established application-metadata convention cannot express.

This increment covers solver-free BDEF bone poses. VMD, complete VPD reproduction with IK/append, advanced skinning, morphs and physics remain mandatory outstanding parts of the overall goal. Synthetic successes do not satisfy representative-model fidelity or the full completion matrix.

## Context

- Baseline: `cc26878912dea54a211fa3d02e6c9fcf29f6eade`. Open Issue and PR collections were empty when inspected.
- `tools/pmx-bdef.ts` preserves `pmxBone.index/name/englishName`; `tools/pmx-to-gltf.ts` stores `metersPerPMXUnit`. Runtime display names are unsuitable identifiers because GLTFLoader sanitizes and uniquifies them.
- [PR #26](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/pull/26), `docs/validation.md` and [existing CI logs](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/39976341487/job/120491809762) report 16 unit/integration tests, seven browser tests, 43 Toon vectors, 109 Outline checks and 12 BDEF comparisons passing; two native-WebGPU cases skipped. These establish existing BDEF behavior, not VPD execution.
- [glTF core](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#skins) supplies joint transforms and inverse binds. Inference: storing the resolved joint transforms while retaining the original binds preserves this bounded posed geometry in ordinary viewers.
- Historical official Three.js [VPD loading](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/r169/examples/jsm/loaders/MMDLoader.js), [parser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/r169/examples/jsm/libs/mmdparser.module.js), [pose helper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/r169/examples/jsm/animation/MMDAnimationHelper.js) and [exporter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/r169/examples/jsm/exporters/MMDExporter.js) provide implementation evidence for text/Shift_JIS handling, named translation/quaternion records, handedness conversion and rest-relative composition. They are alternative-implementation evidence, not a normative VPD specification or measured original-MMD parity. Do not inherit silent unmatched-name skipping or last-duplicate-wins behavior.
- Preserve the earlier evidence-backed documentation correction: old assumption—glTF mandates normalized FLOAT weight sums; correction—§3.7.3.3 uses SHOULD near one. Correct attribution in the affected pipeline/validation documentation while retaining the existing `1e-6` rejection/normalization policy for interoperability, including Three.js loader normalization. No weight acceptance is relaxed.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Document and exercise a supported VPD input profile: byte-based Shift_JIS loading by default and explicit UTF-8 loading, supported comments/newlines/header/record syntax, exact decoded names, record-count validation and finite translation/quaternion values. Reject malformed encoding, truncated records, invalid counts, zero-length or materially invalid quaternions with actionable diagnostics. Specify any roundoff normalization tolerance. Add real byte fixtures rather than testing parsed objects alone; invent no animation or morph channels.
- [ ] Implement model-scoped binding using retained exact source names. Ambiguous target names require an explicit VPD-record-to-PMX-index mapping; never infer PMX identity from `BoneN`, traversal order, sanitized names or English aliases. Validate mappings and repeated target assignments before mutation. Report unmatched names; default to failure unless an explicit partial-application policy is selected. Tests cover reordered records, Japanese/punctuated names, duplicate names, unmatched records, wrong-model application and unchanged state after failure. Treat the parent filename as informational, never an instruction to fetch another file.
- [ ] Define and implement one shared pose contract for converter and runtime: reflect translation Z and quaternion X/Y exactly once, scale translations with the model's retained meters-per-unit, add offsets to original local rest translations and compose rotations relative to original local rest rotations. Restore omitted bones to rest under default replacement semantics. Reapplying A, applying A→B→A and applying from previously modified transforms must not accumulate offsets. Preserve original inverse binds. Reset restores original rest, including after posed-asset reload. Document animation ownership/handoff so a future VMD writer cannot silently accumulate the VPD offsets; test dirty-transform replacement without claiming VMD support.
- [ ] Provide usable converter API and CLI PMX+VPD workflows producing deterministic GLB and unpacked glTF, plus reusable Three.js parse/bind/apply/reset APIs compatible with pinned Three.js `0.186.1`. Recover required scale/baseline metadata after loading and report missing or inconsistent metadata. Preserve source identity, resources, material extensions, fallback and attribution. Existing validator integration reports zero core errors for both output formats. Tests confirm converter and runtime results agree and loading with ordinary GLTFLoader preserves the resolved pose.
- [ ] Commit two distinct attributed VPD poses and two genuinely distinct solver-free BDEF PMX rigs, using original synthetic or lawfully reusable assets. Differences must include geometry or hierarchy, not merely encoding/name variants. Exercise both poses on both rigs through conversion, runtime application, serialization/reload and reset. Independent scalar position/rotation predictions must discriminate handedness, scale and parent/child composition. For sub-meter fixtures retain the existing `2e-6` meter position bound; declare and justify rotation/serialization tolerances before recording results. Assertions must not derive expected results from production pose code.
- [ ] Extend the built Demo with both sample rigs/poses, local VPD file loading with explicit encoding selection, apply/reset controls and clear binding/parser/unsupported-solver diagnostics. Use the reusable APIs. Built-preview Playwright checks cover successful loading, repeated application, pose switching, reset, malformed/ambiguous input and recovery, Toon/PBR switching and outlines. Numerically and visually check posed/reloaded surfaces and outlines against independent baked predictions using the existing raster methodology and justified tolerances. Keep the Gene comparison and existing BDEF regressions working.
- [ ] Update README, pipeline and validation records with executable workflows, metadata/baseline contracts, asset provenance and a per-case result matrix. Identify missing IK/append/physics effects explicitly; do not label raw bone-offset application as full MMD pose reproduction. Distinguish tests present, actually passed, failed, skipped and unperformed. No measured original-MMD VPD evidence currently exists; retain that uncertainty and separate upstream comparison from synthetic conformance.
- [ ] The Coordinator integrates checks into existing `tests/*.test.ts` and Playwright tooling and records passing results for `npm run build` (including asset preparation), `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_CHANNEL=chromium npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:links` and `git diff --check`, using the lockfile and documented Node version. Obtain required dependencies/browser through the existing setup. Preserve justified existing acceptance and raw-weight/normal conventions. Technical requirements may be corrected with primary evidence by retaining the old assumption, corrected requirement, source and rationale; no human approval or independent AI re-review is required. Do not weaken criteria to accommodate unfinished implementation or failing checks.

## Optional validation

Compare solver-disabled results against the historical Three.js helper on the same attributed fixtures. If lawful original-MMD execution becomes available, record controlled pose measurements with renderer/version, assets and tolerances. Native WebGPU execution is useful where an adapter exists. These comparisons must identify their reference limits.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance can be demonstrated before merge with existing local/build-preview tooling. Implementation, testing and ordinary PR review belong to the Coordinator; add no independent AI re-review or generic post-merge rerun.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed MMD/glTF model, VMD animation and
VPD pose reproduction goal. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
